name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Tuesday 2 July 1974

clue.text: Birds bombarded with chaff or flowers?

blocks.note: to rag someone is to tease or chaff them, so those pelted with chaff have been ragged
robins are common garden birds

explanation.surface: Little birds are pelted with husks from a threshing floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads back to front: the ragged comes after the birds in the clue but first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged robin is a pink wildflower of damp meadows with deeply cut, tattered-looking petals.

clue.text: Suite in VIP's train

blocks.note: first meaning: a body of attendants accompanying someone
second meaning: the followers trailing behind an important person

explanation.surface: A grand set of rooms is reserved aboard a dignitary's railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Suite and train both look like hotel rooms and railways; here both mean a group of attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of servants and aides who travel with a monarch or dignitary.

clue.text: Compass of notes early in the passage

blocks.note: surface reading: a navigator's compass with jotted notes
setter's reading: the full range of musical notes, named after the lowest note of the old scale, which sounds first in an ascending run

explanation.surface: Someone describes navigation notes written at the start of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: In medieval music the bottom note of the scale was gamma ut, so the word for the whole range began as the name of the first note.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass here means range, and the word denotes the complete range of musical notes a voice or instrument covers.

clue.text: Wrong to rouse Nero? Awfully!

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly and in disorder, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: It would be a terrible mistake to wake the tyrannical Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erroneous contains an error, so it is mistaken, incorrect or false.

clue.text: Author detailed to do this to his books

definitions.text: to do this to his books

indicators.note: taken as de-tailed, the writer's surname has its final letter cut off

blocks.note: Charles Reade, the Victorian novelist who wrote The Cloister and the Hearth

explanation.surface: A writer describes in detail what should be done with his works.
explanation.walkthrough: Detailed looks like it means thorough, but it is the tail-cutting signal: READE loses its E to give READ.
explanation.definitionFit: What one does to an author's books is peruse them, turning the pages to take in the words.

clue.text: They mix tea and whisky

blocks.note: surface reading: drinkers who lace their cuppa with a dram
setter's reading: the trade professionals who combine different leaves or malts into a house product

explanation.surface: Some people pour a shot of Scotch into their tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea and whisky firms employ specialists who combine varieties to produce a consistent commercial product.

clue.text: Material used in many long dresses

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows, spanning their join

blocks.note: the end of many and the start of long run together
surface padding, completing the picture of clothing

explanation.surface: A synthetic fabric is popular for making full-length frocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Dresses is only surface dressing; the letters sit across the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, a manufactured textile used for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: Jump points and get trapped by these

blocks.note: to spring is to leap
east and south, two compass points

explanation.surface: An animal leaps to certain spots and is caught in snares.
explanation.walkthrough: Points are compass points, a crossword staple for N, E, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Springes are snares made with a noose on a bent sapling, used to catch small game and birds.

clue.text: Man of property, being in the French environment

indicators.note: in places the first element inside what follows it
an environment surrounds something, so the French article wraps around the other part

blocks.note: esse is Latin for being or existence
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A landowner is living somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The French gives LE, which surrounds ESSE, the philosopher's Latin word for being.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds a house or land under a lease, so he is a tenant in possession of property.

clue.text: 'The less wild way of the conqueror

blocks.note: tamer is the comparative of tame, the opposite of wild
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A gentler path is attributed to some victorious warlord.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamerlane, or Timur, was the fourteenth-century Central Asian ruler whose campaigns built a vast empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamerlane is famed as one of history's great military invaders, subduing lands from Persia to India.

clue.text: Falling away of the northern Europeans, say <)

indicators.note: say means as pronounced, so we want a word sounding like the people named

blocks.note: Lapps are the Sami people of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Someone notes the decline of the Nordic peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a decline or backsliding from a standard, as in a lapse in faith or manners.

clue.text: Observer's job is nothing if not hearty

indicators.note: without a heart, so the central letter of the word is removed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a watcher's work amounts to little unless done with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearty usually means enthusiastic; here it is the middle H of the seven letters that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer's task is noticing and recording things, which is what taking note of something means.

clue.text: All said and done, perhaps they impede breathing

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the preceding words are only one possible arrangement of their letters

blocks.note: taken as fodder
taken as fodder

explanation.surface: After everything, these things probably obstruct one's breath.
explanation.walkthrough: All said and done reads as a stock phrase meaning in the end; only two of its words are letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adenoids are lymph tissue at the back of the nose which, when swollen, block the airway in children.

clue.text: Newsman tried-getting round difficulty

indicators.note: in difficulty means in trouble or a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as fodder
a round shape like the letter O

explanation.surface: A journalist made an effort to overcome a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor runs a newspaper or its sections, so he is a senior figure in journalism.

clue.text: One who acquitted himself well as Pope?

blocks.note: first meaning: a guiltless person, who would rightly be acquitted
second meaning: the name taken by thirteen popes

explanation.surface: A pontiff performed his role admirably.
explanation.walkthrough: Acquitted himself well normally means performed creditably; here it suggests being found not guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A blameless person is cleared of a charge, and thirteen pontiffs have reigned under this papal name.

clue.text: Dismiss the members for sport

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
in botany a sport or rogue is a plant that differs abnormally from its type

explanation.surface: Someone sends a club's members away to play games.
explanation.walkthrough: Sport looks athletic but means a freak variant of a plant, which gardeners also call a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue a parliament is to discontinue its session without dissolving it, sending legislators home.

clue.text: Cashing in on Nigel's air of confusion

indicators.note: an air of confusion suggests muddle, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A bewildered Nigel is profiting from something.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an asset is to convert it into money, selling it to obtain its value.

clue.text: Get production of soft steel up sevenfold

indicators.note: production means making something new, so these letters are reworked into a fresh order

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
taken as fodder
taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A mill boss demands output of mild steel be raised seven times.
explanation.definitionFit: Septuple means multiplied by seven, from the Latin root for the number seven.

clue.text: Criminal of note in strange disorder

indicators.note: in disorder means out of place, so the letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: G is a musical note
taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A notorious crook is found in odd chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of an organised criminal gang, such as the mobsters of Prohibition-era Chicago.

clue.text: Highly coloured swimmer, hut not loud

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for the next word is taken away

blocks.note: the garfish is a long thin sea fish with a beak-like snout
f is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A brightly coloured fish lives quietly in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Hut is a misprint for but, a plain link; the fish loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish describes colours that are vivid to the point of gaudiness, loud and showy.

clue.text: Sun god's not out producing fruit

blocks.note: Ra was the Egyptian sun god
the contraction expanded
the opposite of out

explanation.surface: A sun deity remains indoors and makes things grow.
explanation.walkthrough: Fruit is fair since a raisin is a grape dried in the sun, which suits the sun god nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a sweet dried fruit used in baking and cereals.

clue.text: Source of William Morris's 28

blocks.note: surface reading: where the Victorian designer got his intelligence from
setter's reading: 28 is news, and Morris wrote the utopian novel News from ...

explanation.surface: Someone asks where William Morris got his information.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 28 is a synonym for news, so the clue points to the title of Morris's 1890 utopian romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris's utopian novel is titled News from Nowhere, naming the imaginary place where its tidings originate.

clue.text: 25s about foreign noble-men

blocks.note: re means concerning
count is a European title, equivalent to an English earl

explanation.surface: Several clues refer to continental aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is TELL, so 25s means tells, as in narrates.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to narrate it, and tells is the plural verb form matching recounts.

clue.text: Wedding — then Jack goes on the staff

definitions.text: then Jack goes on the staff
definitions.note: describes the word rather than defining it: add Jack and it becomes a flag flown on a staff

blocks.note: first meaning: the joining of two people in marriage

blocks.clueFragment: then Jack goes on the staff
blocks.note: second meaning: followed by Jack, it names the British flag hoisted on a flagpole

explanation.surface: After a marriage, Jack joins the employees of the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like workers, but it is a flagstaff; the Union Jack is the British national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is a joining of two people, and the word also forms the name of the British flag.

clue.text: "But, soft! what light through yonder breaks'.'" (? R and J)

blocks.clueFragment: But, soft! what light through yonder breaks
blocks.note: surface reading: Romeo's balcony speech with one word missing
setter's reading: supply the word from Romeo and Juliet that completes the quotation

explanation.surface: Romeo gazes up at Juliet's balcony and marvels at the light.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line in Act 2 is: But, soft! what light through yonder window breaks?
explanation.definitionFit: The gap in Shakespeare's line is filled by the opening in a wall through which Juliet's light shines.

clue.text: Outlet for brains?

blocks.note: surface reading: a place where clever people can show their talent
setter's reading: clever people leaving the country in numbers, as if flowing away down a pipe

explanation.surface: Someone asks where intelligent people can find an outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The brain drain was the 1960s term for scientists leaving Britain for better pay abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet pipe carries water away, and the brain drain phrase applies this to departing talent.

clue.text: Give instruction to an archer

blocks.note: first meaning: to order someone to do something
second meaning: William, the Swiss crossbowman of legend

explanation.surface: Someone coaches a bowman.
explanation.walkthrough: William Tell shot an apple from his son's head with a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: To command someone is to order them, and the legendary Swiss marksman bore this surname.

clue.text: Wilderness, first rate do

blocks.note: to do wrong, taken loosely as a wrongdoing
A1 means first-class, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A desert party is described as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: A do is also a party, which is the surface sense; the pieces are written in reverse order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wilderness of Sinai is the desert where the Israelites wandered after the Exodus, in the Bible.

clue.text: What is stated to be foolish talk about shaking dice

indicators.note: shaking scrambles things, so these letters come out in a new order
about means around, so one part surrounds the other

blocks.note: to prate is to chatter idly
the letters of dice shaken up

explanation.surface: Talk of rolling dice is said to be silly.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar and logic, the predicate is the part of a sentence or proposition that affirms something about the subject.

clue.text: In a word no US news

blocks.clueFragment: In a word no US news
blocks.note: surface reading: a remark that there is nothing to report from America
setter's reading: one word for news, also the I in the American CIA

explanation.surface: Someone reports briefly that America has sent no word.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears garbled in print; news is the definition, and intelligence is both information and what US agencies gather.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence is information received, especially secret military or political information gathered by agents.
